object_context: For a mild bounded ancient 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes solution on R^3 x (-infinity,0) with finite Albritton–Barker Type-I quantity I=sup_Q(A+C+D+E), test whether the standard local-energy ledger itself supplies a scale-decaying, telescoping, monotone, or otherwise summable charge across dynamically realized dyadic scale descendants, strong enough to obstruct indefinite critical-mass replication without assuming global L3, orbit compactness, or a smallest singular scale.
structural_coordinates: Navier-Stokes scaling u_lambda(x,t)=lambda u(lambda x,lambda^2 t)
A,C,D,E are dimensionless under parabolic scaling
physical local kinetic energy on radius R scales as R
space-time |u|^3 and |p-mean|^(3/2) on Q_R scale as R^2
standard cutoff derivatives scale as |grad phi_R|=O(R^-1) and |partial_t phi_R|+|Delta phi_R|=O(R^-2)
the normalized local-energy ledger therefore has no automatic positive power of R
nested cylinders may reuse the same physical core and are not disjoint events
pressure is nonlocal but a time-dependent spatial mean may be subtracted in the local-energy pressure-work term
infinite dyadic descent is compatible with geometrically shrinking physical charges unless a dimensionless monotone/no-recrossing mechanism is proved
Type-II remains a sibling residual even if this Type-I child closes
equivalent_formulations: Scale-charge form: find a dimensionless Q_j on scales R_j=2^-j R_0 with sum_j Q_j<infinity or a strict monotone drop on every realized descendant.
No-recrossing form: show that once a critical threshold is spent at one scale, sufficiently smaller nested scales cannot cross the same threshold except through a separately charged event.
Telescoping form: express shell/time flux as F(R_j)-F(R_{j+1}) with F bounded below and a quantitatively useful drop at each descendant.
Hostile-check form: determine whether finite I plus the standard local-energy inequality yields only O(1) normalized cost per scale; if so, retire naive summation.

solved_analogues.what_works: Uniform global L3 control along t_k->-infinity activates a Liouville theorem.
solved_analogues.missing_here: finite I does not provide global L3 tail tightness.

solved_analogues.what_works: small enough scale-invariant local quantities imply regularity, so singular behavior forces repeated failure of a smallness condition.
solved_analogues.missing_here: failure of smallness at nested scales is not automatically a disjoint or nonsummable physical expenditure.

near_solved_analogues.method: convert failure of regularity into a minimal orbit compact modulo symmetries, then use rigidity.
near_solved_analogues.disanalogy: finite I is local-parabolic control, not a frozen global critical norm with an established Navier-Stokes minimal-element theory for this atom.

falsifier may refute only an inference from standard bounds, never existence of a target PDE solution
difference_witness.cheapest_repeat_failure_test: perform exact scaling bookkeeping on every term in the standard local-energy inequality under finite A,C,D,E and test whether the dimensionless per-scale bound gains any decay in R

explicit_disanalogies: A scale-neutral bookkeeping failure is not a Navier-Stokes counterexample.
A forward DSS suitable solution is not a backward Type-I ancient witness and cannot refute the target theorem.
Physical shell charges shrinking like R or R^2 can be summable even when a dimensionless threshold is repeatedly crossed; finite physical total is not a well-founded scale rank.
An O(1) upper bound per scale does not prove that actual flux is O(1) below, nor does it exclude cancellation or telescoping.
No pressure estimate may assume the global L3 conclusion or tail compactness it is meant to prove.
counterexample_first_falsifier: Use scale bookkeeping before any theorem invention: under A,C,D,E<=M on Q(2R), estimate the standard local-energy cutoff terms and ask whether the normalized bound contains a positive power of R, a sign, or a telescoping defect. If none appears, naive per-scale charging is structurally insufficient.
